elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: New 21.4 says only "shall indemnify Teleglobe against any claim"; there is no "defend" (or "hold harmless") obligation and no reference to affiliates. Retained 21.2 gives the indemnifying Party only a right to "observe but not directly participate", so no defence duty exists anywhere.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 21.4 runs in favour of "Teleglobe" alone; affiliates are not named or included.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: 21.4: indemnity "against any claim by a third party that such part, equipment or software infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right" for any part of APCN 2 or equipment/software provided, procured or supplied by the other Party.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: No breach-of-law trigger appears in 21.4 or in retained 21.2 (which is limited to claims against a Party "as an owner of APCN 2").

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No unauthorised-access/disclosure of Customer Data trigger in the inserted or retained language.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: No gross negligence or wilful misconduct trigger in 21.4.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: 21.4 contains no notice mechanic; retained 21.2 addresses only observation rights and share-limited contribution.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: No allocation of defence control; 21.2's "observe but not directly participate" language is left untouched and is not a control allocation in our favour.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Mutual 21.2 is retained unchanged, so Teleglobe still indemnifies every other Party for all third-party claims against them as owners of APCN 2 \u2014 far broader than Customer content and Customer breach of law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Inserted 21.4 obliges "Each other Party which provides, procures or supplies any part of APCN 2, or any equipment or software used therein" to indemnify Teleglobe against third-party claims of IP infringement or misappropriation. In this multilateral consortium the other Parties are the supplying counterparties, so the indemnity runs in the correct direction.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: "save to the extent the claim arises from modifications made by Teleglobe".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: "from combination by Teleglobe with items not so provided".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: "shall, at its option, procure for Teleglobe the right to continue using the infringing item, or modify or replace it" \u2014 an affirmative obligation with election among the three remedies.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: "if none of those remedies is reasonably available shall refund the fees paid by Teleglobe in respect of the infringing item" \u2014 conditioned on unavailability, as the element requires.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: "aggregate liability under this Subparagraph 21.4 shall not exceed three times the annual fees and costs payable by Teleglobe under this Agreement." Multiplier matches; "and costs" is used because consideration under this consortium agreement is expressed as cost-share contributions rather than fees, so the base is not an unnecessary expansion.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Duplicate element string in checklist; see above \u2014 met by inserted 21.4.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the single inserted Subparagraph 21.4 delivers the IP indemnity, all three customary exclusions (Teleglobe modifications, combinations, specifications), the procure/modify/replace remedy ladder, a conditional refund of fees paid for the infringing item, and a 3\u00d7 annual super-cap expressed as a cap on aggregate liability under that subparagraph.

Preferred level is not reached and was not targeted: no duty to defend, no affiliate coverage, no breach-of-law, data-breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers, no notice/control/cooperation procedure, and the mutual 21.2 indemnity given by us is untouched rather than narrowed to Customer content and Customer breach of law.

Minimality holds: the redline is a pure insertion of one subparagraph, deletes nothing (including nothing favourable), adds no survival tail, at-own-expense language, extra damages categories or procedural boilerplate, and does not duplicate 21.2, which addresses a different subject (third-party claims against a Party as owner of APCN 2, share-limited under Schedule B).

Intent is preserved: 21.2's share-limited contribution scheme, the Paragraph 32 claims-settlement machinery and the 4.9 supplier/Wet Segment disclaimers all continue to operate; the new cap is self-contained ("under this Subparagraph 21.4") so it does not disturb any general liability allocation, and no term is left undefined or dangling.

Drafting caution (not a defect on the record shown): confirm no existing Subparagraph 21.4 in Paragraph 21 so the new number does not collide with a retained provision; if one exists, renumber the insertion.

Optional strengthening if the counterparties will engage: add "defend and hold harmless", extend the beneficiary to Teleglobe's affiliates, and add notice/control/cooperation mechanics to move from the fallback toward the preferred position.
